summary: The change strengthens the trust boundary rather than weakening it. Grantability is carried authoritatively (JSON-encoded in the terminal error so a free-text reason cannot spoof Grantable:/Recovery: markers) and the card offers a durable approval only when grantable === true, failing closed on undefined (no legacy compat path). Hard boundaries (protected-capability, memory, settings denylist, locked-preset/fixed-image) are never turned into an approvable grant. Side effects are fenced after cancellation across all tool paths (facade, third-party MCP, shell) so a late-resolving approval cannot launch a command after a sibling denial terminated the turn. Adding an under-declared tool to a job on approval is a human-initiated edit, consistent with decision 0106 (scheduled runs cannot self-mutate).
non_blocking_findings: Pre-check denials route to a non-grantable instruction card on scheduled runs, so a hard-boundary denial can never be presented as approvable.
residual_risks: Grant (permission store) and requirement append (job store) are intentionally non-atomic; the residual grant-without-requirement gap is benign (agent has the tool; job runs) and self-heals on the next denial. Tracked as D-0050.
